opening_message:
Ticket 1: Belinda Fuentes (employee ID E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E039.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write unless their role owns the system; Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is not permitted. Granting write as the maximum allowed.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E039 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training are limited to read on any system (never admin). Admin request exceeds the maximum, so grant read.
reason: E039 requested admin to Payroll. The Security DB note identifies E039 as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors with basic training are limited to read on any system and never admin. Even under the HR note (full-time Analyst), admin would exceed the max (write, since Analyst does not own Payroll). Because the request exceeds the maximum under the more restrictive, security-backed record (contractor/basic), the maximum allowed is read. Never grant more than requested; grant the maximum of read.
